subject: Computer Networking
title: Antenna Types and Patterns
description: A 60-second lesson on Antenna Types and Patterns.

hook.text: An antenna doesn't create energy. It focuses it. The shape determines where the signal goes.

buildup.text: Omnidirectional antennas radiate in all directions like a donut. Used for general indoor coverage.

discovery.text: Directional antennas focus signal one way like a flashlight. Used for point-to-point long-range links.

twist.text: MIMO uses multiple antennas at once. Each sends a different data stream, multiplying throughput.

climax.text: Beamforming adjusts antenna patterns dynamically, focusing energy toward each client for better range.

punchline.text: The antenna shapes the signal. The right one changes everything.

quiz.question: What does beamforming do?
options: Dynamically focuses the wireless signal toward each client
Blocks signals from reaching outside the building
Converts wireless signals to fiber optic light

details.summary: Network antennas come in omnidirectional, directional, and sector varieties, each radiating signals in different patterns. Omnidirectional antennas cover all directions equally, while directional antennas focus energy in a narrow beam for long-range point-to-point links.
details.whyItMatters: Antenna selection determines wireless coverage shape, range, and signal strength. Choosing the wrong antenna type wastes power and creates coverage gaps or unwanted interference.
takeaways: Omnidirectional antennas broadcast equally in all horizontal directions
Directional antennas focus signals for long-range point-to-point links
Antenna gain is measured in dBi and indicates signal focus

faq.question: What is antenna gain?
faq.answer: Gain measures how much an antenna focuses energy in a particular direction, expressed in dBi. A higher gain does not create more power — it concentrates existing power into a narrower beam. A 9 dBi directional antenna reaches farther than a 3 dBi omnidirectional but covers a smaller area.

faq.question: Which antenna type is best for outdoor Wi-Fi?
faq.answer: For covering a wide area like a courtyard, use an omnidirectional antenna mounted high. For connecting two buildings, use directional antennas pointed at each other. Sector antennas cover a 60 to 120-degree arc and are used on cell towers and stadium installations.
